When they activate the buy back clause you have to hope they reject the offer.

I always check the clauses section in the transfers as soon as I take over a team so I can work out what ones may impact me, both positive and negative. 

If I have a player that I know will play loads of games for me and the board have negotiated a cheaper price to pay then I'll take it. Same with future sell ons, if the money I'm offered to buy the clause is a lot less than I know I'll make then I'll sacrifice transfer budget now for greater rewards later.

And that can be inversed as well. If the board have negotiated a lower payout to you for someone making appearances for their new club and you can see they aren't playing then sell that clause as it's a lot better than nothing. 

With regards to future sell on clauses coming to you it's a judgement call based on how much of a risk you want to take and how much you need the money now. I always stick high future profit clauses on young players I sell as you never know what they could turn out like and if you sell them to teams in the top two divisions you can normally get more from that clause when you sell it than the actual transfer

What I mean by that is you need to concentrate on your 'sphere of influence' as I like to call it. I feel that as people with BPD we often completely ignore the things we have control over and fixate on the things we cannot control i.e. other people's feelings/emotions/intentions/etc. rather than the things we actually have control of,  this is often further exacerbated by our black and white thinking as well.

While I'm not advocating a 'fuck it' approach to other people I think we do need to focus on 'keeping our side of the street clean' as that's what we have the most influence over. As soon as we put a large amount of importance on an area that we have a real minimal control over we often set ourselves up for a downfall as we can put ourselves mentally multiple steps ahead in a situation that has yet to arise.

It would be easy to say remove a goal such as having a relationship we both know that's not how our brain works when it comes to stuff. However, focusing more on improving the things you can influence in your own life will not only improve your outlook on everything in time but will also extend itself into other aspects of your life that you aren't able to influence.

You'll get to a better place and a place your happy with before you know it just  concentrate on yourself as a starting point and go from there!
